summary: The PR adds options that state their ends, causes on fixes, class links and deferral of left calls. The new checks are tight, the docs and the version bump are in place, and every changed file under the Docs step has its entry. Two findings are correctness. The 0.5.0 upgrade note promises a review-dial stop replays whole, but the first review on a PR with an earlier Redline run now reruns. And the forcing point can turn a shaper's ordinary call into a left call that the new draft check then stops. The four nits concern the new checks' and prompts' wording and reach: errors that name only the first fault, a warning with a false reason, a human pass told of an own-file rule it never applies, and a one-place match stricter than its sibling message. Nothing here touches scheduled or queued work.

findings.title: The 0.5.0 note says a review-dial stop replays whole, but on a PR with an earlier Redline run the first review reruns
findings.description:
The new section "A stopped run across 0.5.0" makes three claims: a stopped run replays everything before its first shape, a run stopped at the review dial "replays whole and goes on", and any later stop "replays its gather, review and post". The PR description makes the same promise ("A stop at the review dial replays whole"). None of them holds on a pull request that already has a Redline round with a finding in a disposition other than none or not-changed.

Why: on such a PR `trackedList` (workflows/redline-loop.js:109) is non-empty, so `showsEarlier` (1850) is true for the run's first, whole-PR review. That review now appends LINK_ASK (1929-1931) and is called with REVIEW_SCHEMA_LINKS (3081-3087). origin/main has no `sameClassAs` anywhere. Replay follows the prompt sequence (agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md, points 1 and 23), so after the update that review reruns.

The post reruns too, because its prompt embeds the content of the review file and the findings file (postPrompt, 2206-2216). It overwrites `round-<n>-review.json` and `round-<n>-findings.json` with the rerun's findings. `has-review` then exits 0, so the post is skipped as already posted, and the agent maps the posted comments to findings by their `**R<n>-` prefix (2200). The rerun reviewer is not deterministic, so its R2-1 can be a different finding from the R2-1 that was posted. The thread replies, the shape and the review dial's `args.selected` (which names the posted ids) then work from the rerun's findings while GitHub shows the old ones.

Correction to the candidate: `commentIds` is not `{}`. The skipped post maps the posted ids by prefix.

The spec's own measurement (shape.md, "A review-dial stop replays whole (3 of 3)") used scenarios with no earlier round. The PR description's prompt table already records the change: "A review that is shown earlier findings | 467 | 467" differ.

Conditions for the failure: an earlier Redline run on the PR left a dispositioned finding; the run stopped anywhere after its first review was posted; the plugin was updated across 0.5.0 before the relaunch; the repository is not the plugin's own (there #81 runs the script the run launched with).
findings.proposedFix: In docs/upgrading.md, "A stopped run across 0.5.0", say that on a pull request that already carries a Redline round whose findings have a disposition, the first review's prompt changed too. Such a run reruns its review and post (the post is skipped as already posted, and the round's findings file is rewritten from the rerun), so it must be finished or restarted before updating. Keep "replays whole" only for a pull request with no earlier round. Correct the PR description's "A stop at the review dial replays whole" the same way.

findings.title: A human review pass's shape prompts say an own-file call is left to the person and drafted, which never applies in that pass
findings.description:
OPTIONS_ASK (1126) interpolates LEFT_CALL (1125). It is sent in the Return sentence of humanShapePrompt (2319) and of the human pass's reshape prompt (2356). Its own-file clause ("one on a file of Redline's own"; in a repository with no ask rules, all of LEFT_CALL) tells the human pass's shaper that such a call is left to the person and that its defer option carries a draft. Neither holds in a human pass: forceAskRules records an own-file call only when `!pass.human` (3773), and HUMAN_WHY (447) has no "redline's own file", so no such call ever reaches `record.forced`. A shaper that follows the clause and drafts that option has the draft dropped with a warning by checkOptions (3596-3600). The shaper file's rule 8 ("Rule 7 stands") points the same way.

The candidate's further claim does not hold: the author is not filed an issue other than the one shown. The draft is deleted before the hand-off returns the calls (4273), so the author sees no draft. A pick that ends in defer gets the resolve agent's draft, which a human pass raises at its draft stop (raisesDrafts, 4211) before anything is filed. The cost is a draft written for nothing and a warning in the run.
findings.proposedFix: Build the human pass's options sentence without the own-file clause: name only a finding a repository ask rule covers, and in a repository with no rules give no left-call clause at all. Pin it with a loop case: a human pass's shape prompt in a repository with no rules contains no "file of Redline's own" text.

findings.title: A revise-only pass clears a sameClassAs link with a false reason: the earlier finding was recorded
findings.description:
A revise-only pass (`/redline:redline-revise <pr> round <N>`) is launched with `priorFindings: []` (skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:26). It calls `honourLinks(round, record.findings, true)` (5701) before its record joins `rounds` (5702). For a link the findings file carries, linkFault (3021-3032) finds the id in neither `rounds` nor `priorById` and returns "<id> names no finding Redline recorded on this pull request". The run then warns, for example, "the reviewer linked R2-1 to R1-1 as one class (sameClassAs), but R1-1 names no finding Redline recorded on this pull request; the link is cleared".

That is false whenever the file was written by a run that held the record:
- `/redline:redline-review` follows the full precheck, so on a PR with an earlier round it passes prior-findings, keeps a link to an earlier run's fixed finding, and writes it into round-<N>-findings.json (3289).
- A full run's fix-diff round keeps a link to its own round 1 the same way.

The clearing itself is the spec's decision 41 (shape.md: a link "a revise-only pass reads from an earlier run's findings file ... its record cannot show the fix"), and tests/loop-test.mjs:5058-5059 pins the warning text. One effect is a fact for the shaper: on this path the class rule does not apply, and an `instance` fix for the finding passes checkCauses (3650-3653). The candidate calls the drop silent; it is not, since the warning is printed, but the reason the warning gives is wrong.
findings.proposedFix: Give linkFault the revise-only case its own reason, for example "this revise-only pass holds no record of earlier rounds to check it against", and update the case at tests/loop-test.mjs:5059. Whether a revise-only launch should pass prior-findings so that such a link stands is a separate choice.

findings.title: An ordinary call the forcing point puts under a paths rule stops the round on its undrafted defer option
findings.description:
When the shaper already wrote a call for a finding, forceAskRules keeps it and rewrites only `why_human` (3803, 3823-3825), then records the finding in `record.forced` (3831-3833). checkOptions runs after it (vetShape, 4167 then 4183). For every forced call it throws an ownCheck stop at `shape` on any option that ends in defer without a complete draft (3591-3595).

An ordinary call's defer option has no draft, by the shaper's own instructions: OPTIONS_ASK (1126) says "no other option carries one", and the example call in agents/redline-shaper.md is exactly Full fix / Mitigate (ends defer, no draft) / Accept. So the round stops when the shaper writes such a call (with `why_human` "outside the pull request", say) for a finding whose file, or whose recommended change's files, a paths rule covers.

What this needs: the shaper did not treat the finding as rule-covered. Either it missed the rule the rules block (661) gave it, which is the case the forcing point exists to absorb, or it read the glob differently from ruleForPaths, which folds case and `..` segments (638-651).

origin/main has no such check, so the same output was forced and the round went on. Now, on guided, it is one more stop and relaunch; on autopilot the run ends in an error at `shape` and a person has to relaunch it. Nothing is lost: the resume reruns the shaper with the error, which names the call as one left to the person. The node harness is refused to the reviewer role, so this is traced, not run.
findings.proposedFix: Record at 3823-3825 that the call was the shaper's ordinary call made left by the forcing point. For such a call, do not require a draft at 3592. Either keep the option undrafted and let the resolve agent write the draft after a pick, the path 4416-4433 already takes when the call offers no draft, or drop the undrafted defer option with a warning. Add a loop case: a shaper call with `why_human` "outside the pull request" and an undrafted Mitigate option, whose files a paths rule covers, reaches the hand-off.

findings.title: checkCauses and checkOptions name only the first failure, costing one relaunch per fault
findings.description:
Both new checks stop at the first problem they find:
- checkCauses (3620-3655) loops over the shaper's fixes and throws at the first one with no usable cause (3630-3632), a `where` outside the repository (3634-3636), a one-place miss (3638-3640), an unusable sweep (3646-3648) or an instance under a link (3651-3653).
- checkOptions (3574-3603) throws at the first call with a bad option (3579-3581), a repeated label (3584-3586), a `recommended` that names no option (3588-3590) or an undrafted defer option on a left call (3593-3595).

When one of these stops a reshape, the resume line tells the rerun to "correct what the error names" (resumeLine, 744). A reshape that returned two fixes with no cause is therefore told about R1-1 only, corrects it, and stops again on R1-2. agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md (line 19) says a stop whose resume line says that "names every failure of its check in one error, since each one it leaves out is one more relaunch" (#114, R4-6). On a round's first shape the resume rewrites from scratch and may fix the rest unprompted, but the error still names one.

The pattern predates this PR: checkDrafts and checkWhy on origin/main throw at the first failure too. The two new checks repeat it. The cost is one relaunch per further fault; nothing is lost.
findings.proposedFix: Collect every failing fix in checkCauses and every failing call in checkOptions, each with all of its faults, and throw one checkError listing them all, as checkDeclineReasons (3662-3665) and checkCalls' noCall (3522-3525) already do. Add a loop case: a reshape with two fixes with no cause stops with an error that names both.

findings.title: The one-place check requires an exact task file, while the outside-path stop beside it says `where` may be a folder
findings.description:
The one-place check passes only when `repoPath(cause.where).path` is exactly one of the task's cleaned files (3633, 3637-3640). It stops the round at `shape` even when the task changes the place named, if `where` is:
- a folder: `app/Services/` reads as `app/Services` (pathSegments, 511-524);
- a path with a line suffix: repoPath keeps `app/x.php:42` whole.

The contract for one-place asks for a file: CAUSE_ASK (1129, "so where is one of its files") and the shaper's rule 3 ("`where` is one of the task's files"). For every outcome, `where` is "a path in the repository". But the outside-path stop beside it (3635) tells the shaper "where names the file or folder the cause lives in" whatever the outcome. A one-place fix resumed after that stop can therefore be steered to a folder and stopped again at 3638. Each is a resumable ownCheck stop and nothing is lost; the cost is a relaunch.
findings.proposedFix: Word the outside-path message by outcome: for one-place, "names one of the task's files"; otherwise, a file or a folder. Either strip a trailing `:<line>` before the match, or name the accepted form in CAUSE_ASK. Whether a folder holding a task file should satisfy one-place is a contract choice; today the contract says it does not.

list.summary: The 0.5.0 upgrade note says a run stopped at the review dial replays whole, and that any later stop replays its gather, review and post. Neither holds on a pull request that already had a Redline run (trackedList not empty). There the first review's prompt now carries LINK_ASK and its schema is REVIEW_SCHEMA_LINKS (showsEarlier is true for reviewed 'pr' with tracked prior findings), so the review reruns instead of replaying. Fix: correct the note to say such a run reruns its first review, so it must be finished or restarted before updating, and drop the 'replays whole' claim for that case.
list.failure_scenario: A PR with an earlier Redline run is stopped at the review dial, the plugin is updated to 0.5.0, and the run is relaunched as the doc allows. The reviewer reruns and returns different findings. The post step's has-review check sees round N already posted and skips ('already posted'), so commentIds is {}. The run then shapes, builds and replies (as issue comments) about findings that were never posted, and args.selected names ids from the old review.

list.summary: This adds a hard stop that the shaper hits even after following its own prompt. The shaper writes an ordinary ask (for example 'outside the pull request') whose 'Mitigate' option ends in defer and, as OPTIONS_ASK says ('no other option carries one'), has no draft. A paths rule then matches the finding's file or its task files, forceAskRules makes the call a left call by rewriting only its why_human, and checkOptions throws an ownCheck error. Fix: on a call that forceAskRules made left (one the shaper did not write as left), do not require the draft. Keep the option undrafted and let the resolve agent write the draft, as the typed-defer path already does (`optionDraft` unset, resolve-written entry checked by `undrafted`), or drop that option with a warning.
list.failure_scenario: askRules has paths `config/project/**`. The shaper sorts R1-1 as ask with why_human 'outside the pull request' and options Full fix/Mitigate(defer, no draft)/Accept, and its files list config/project/x.yaml. forceAskRules sets record.forced[R1-1], and checkOptions throws 'the shaper gave R1-1, a call for a finding left to the person, an option that ends in defer with no complete drafted issue'. Before this change the round went on; on autopilot it now ends in an error at shape and needs a relaunch.

list.summary: checkOptions and checkCauses each stop on the first failing call or finding, and within one call on the first failing check, so a shaper result with several faults costs one relaunch per fault. agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md (#114, R4-6) says a stop whose resume line says 'correct what the error names' names every failure of its check in one error. checkCauses (line 3620) loops over fixes and throws on the first missing or bad cause, and checkOptions throws per call. Fix: collect every faulty call or finding (and every fault within each) and raise one checkError listing them all.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper returns two fixes with no cause (R1-1, R1-2). The stop names only R1-1, the resume tells the shaper to correct what the error names, and it fixes R1-1. The relaunch then stops again for R1-2: two relaunches where one would do. The same happens for two calls with bad options.

list.summary: A revise-only pass (`/redline-revise <pr> round N`) gets `priorFindings: []` and an empty `rounds`, so honourLinks clears every sameClassAs link in the findings file. The warning it prints, '<id> names no finding Redline recorded on this pull request', is false: the review run that wrote the file had checked the link against prior-findings. The class rule (#75) is also silently dropped on the review-then-revise path. Fix: word the warning for this case as 'this pass holds no record of earlier rounds to check it against', or pass prior-findings to a revise-only launch so links that held still hold.
list.failure_scenario: `/redline-review` on round 2 keeps R2-1 sameClassAs [R1-1] because R1-1 was fixed. `/redline-revise <pr> round 2` then warns 'R1-1 names no finding Redline recorded on this pull request', clears the link, and lets R2-1 be fixed as one more instance.

list.summary: LEFT_CALL, shared by every shape prompt, tells the shaper that a call on Redline's own files is left to the person and that its defer option carries a draft. That is also sent to a human review pass's shaper, but in a human pass no own-file call is ever forced: the ownCall check requires !pass.human, and HUMAN_WHY has no OWN_FILE. A draft written there is dropped with a warning, and an author who picks that option is filed a draft written by the resolve agent, not the one they were shown. Fix: build the human pass's sentence from askRules alone, and leave the own-file clause out of humanShapePrompt and the human reshape prompt.
list.failure_scenario: Human pass, a comment on `.claude/redline.json`. The shaper follows the prompt and puts a draft on the call's defer option. checkOptions sees left false and warns that the draft is dropped. The author picks the option, and an issue different from the one shown in the call is filed.

list.summary: The one-place check needs `where` to be exactly one of the task's files. A `where` naming a folder, which the outside-path error message invites ('where names the file or folder the cause lives in'), or a path with a line suffix ('app/x.php:42') stops the round even when the fix touches that place. Fix: make the messages agree (one-place names a file), and accept a `where` that is a task file once a `:<line>` suffix is removed, or a folder that holds one of the task's files.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper returns cause {where: 'app/Services/', outcome: 'one-place'} with files ['app/Services/Normaliser.php'], or where 'app/x.php:42' with files ['app/x.php']. checkCauses throws 'its task's files ... do not include app/Services', an ownCheck stop and a relaunch for a correct fix.
